policies.title: SEMO - International undergraduate admission policies and guidelines (deadlines, English minimums, score codes)

test_policy.notes: Test scores are optional for admission on the first-year international page; they may qualify for merit scholarships and are used for math/English placement. SAT EBRW 450+ or ACT English and Reading 21+ can also serve as English proof. The Common Data Set says 'Test optional'.

requirements.notes: Own online application; $60 non-refundable international fee, no waivers. No minimum high school GPA is stated for first-year international applicants (the acceptance letter lists conditions). Unofficial transcripts and English scores are enough at application; official ones are needed after admission. NACES/AICE credential evaluations are accepted for first-time freshmen. After admission: Affidavit of Financial Support and bank statement covering estimated annual cost minus scholarship; no tuition deposit. Nursing and some programs have higher English standards. Common Data Set admission factors: GPA and rigor very important, test scores and class rank considered, essay and recommendations not considered.

deadlines.label: Priority date (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The Common Data Set lists a priority date of Dec 1 and an application closing date of July 1; no year is printed, so the fall 2027 cycle is assumed. What the priority date affects is not explained.

deadlines.label: International fall 2027 application deadline (regular)
deadlines.notes: Fall (August) deadline is July 1; students applying web-only or already holding a valid US visa have July 15. No year is printed, so fall 2027 is assumed.

deadlines.label: International spring 2027 (January) application deadline (regular)
deadlines.notes: Spring deadline is November 1 (November 15 for web-only or valid-US-visa applicants); no year printed, so spring 2027 entry is assumed.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Proof can be a test score, a US high school diploma, O/A-level, WAEC, IB (English-medium), a US-accredited international school diploma, a secondary diploma from a listed English-official country, SAT EBRW 450 / ACT English and Reading 21, or Level 5 of SEMO's Intensive English Program. Scores must be official and sent by the test provider. Conditionally admitted students may submit official scores by the last office day before classes start.

english.notes: For tests taken before Jan 21, 2026. English Program Pathway applicants (conditional/IEP route): 52-60.
Tests on or after Jan 21, 2026; the page prints 3.5 (pathway 3.0) without naming the scale, presumably the new 1-6 scale; confirm with admissions.
Academic or Express. Pathway applicants: 40-43. Also accepted: Michigan English Test 48 (pathway 45), iTEP 3.7, Oxford ELLT 6 (pathway 5).

aid.notes: Automatic merit awards at admission, no separate application: International Academic Award $8,850 per year for freshmen with a 3.25 high school GPA (it covers the nonresident-minus-domestic tuition gap, estimated at 15 hours per semester; renewable up to 4 years with 2.75 GPA and 24 credit hours per year; also for the IEP pathway), or International Student Scholarship $2,000 per year for a 2.5 GPA. No international need-based aid was found on the scholarships page. Common Data Set: 467 nonresidents received institutional aid, average $8,011.

toefl.note: Official score code on the international policies page; scores must be sent electronically by the test provider.

ielts.note: No numeric IELTS code is listed; official scores must be sent by the test provider.
